title: Systems of coherent modules on the thickenings X_n are coherent formal modules on X
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ ($n\ge0$), $X\to S$ a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X_n=X\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change] with the closed immersions $j_n:X_n\to X$ and $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ ($j_{n+1}i_n=j_n$), and $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf generated by $I$ (the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to\mathcal O_X$ for the structure morphism $f:X\to S$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]). Then: (1) $X$ is Noetherian and $j_n$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. (2) Let $\mathrm{Sys}$ be the category of systems $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules $\mathcal F_n$ [pqf-def-coherent] and isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ [def-pc-module-pullback], a morphism $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)\to(\mathcal G_n,\varphi'_n)$ being a family of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-linear $u_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$ with $u_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi'_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$. The functor sending $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ to the inverse system $(j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1})_{n\ge1}$, whose transition map $j_{n,*}\mathcal F_n\to j_{n,*}i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}=j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ is $j_{n,*}$ of the map $\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ adjoint to $\varphi_{n-1}$, is an equivalence of categories $\mathrm{Sys}\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. (3) For a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, the system $(\mathcal F|_{X_n},c_n)$, $\mathcal F|_{X_n}=j_n^*\mathcal F$ and $c_n:i_n^*(\mathcal F|_{X_{n+1}})\cong\mathcal F|_{X_n}$ the canonical isomorphisms, is sent to an object isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$, by the isomorphisms $j_{n,*}j_n^*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F$, naturally in $\mathcal F$; hence for coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ the families $(u_n:\mathcal G|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ with $u_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$ correspond bijectively to the morphisms $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, the family $(u|_{X_n})_n$ of an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ corresponding to $u^\wedge$, and an isomorphism $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong(j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1})_n$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ corresponds to isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$. (4) For a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module $\mathcal F_0$ one has $\operatorname{Supp}(j_{0,*}\mathcal F_0)=j_0(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_0)$, and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$ (for $X_0\to S_0$) if and only if $j_0(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S$ (for $X\to S$) [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; so the equivalence of (2) identifies the systems with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ proper over $S_0$ with $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$.

proof.text: (1), $X$ is Noetherian. $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian (the one-member affine cover $\{S\}$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]). The morphism $f:X\to S$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type, so $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; and $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] while $S$ (the spectrum of a ring) is quasi-compact, so $X=f^{-1}(S)$ is quasi-compact. Thus $X$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); Morphisms Lemma 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex

proof.text: (1), the closed immersions $j_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1) to $f$ and $K=I^{n+1}$: $X_n=X_{I^{n+1}}$ and $j_n$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is $I^{n+1}\mathcal O_X$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (2) $I^{n+1}\mathcal O_X=(I\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}=\mathcal I^{n+1}$ (powers as in [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]). This is (1). Moreover, for an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $X$ with $B$ Noetherian, $j_n^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B/I^{n+1}B)$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1) with $B/I^{n+1}B$ Noetherian; these opens cover $X_n$ (the $U$ cover $X$, step 1), and $X_n$ is quasi-compact, being homeomorphic to the closed subset $j_n(X_n)$ of the quasi-compact $X$. So every $X_n$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; in particular coherent modules on $X$ and on $X_n$ are exactly the quasi-coherent modules of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); Schemes Lemma 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion), literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex

proof.text: (The closed immersions $i_n$ and the ideals $\mathcal I_n$.) For $n\ge1$ let $\mathcal I_n=I\mathcal O_{X_n}$ (for $X_n\to S$). By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (3) with $J=I^{n+1}\subseteq J'=I^n$, the morphism $i_{n-1}:X_{n-1}\to X_n$ (the unique one with $j_n\circ i_{n-1}=j_{n-1}$ over $S_{n-1}\to S_n$, which is the $i_{n-1}$ of the statement) is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $I^n\mathcal O_{X_n}=\mathcal I_n^n$ ([lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (2) for $X_n\to S$). By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (4), the ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_n}$ (image of $j_n^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{X_n}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]) is $\mathcal I_n$. Finally, pushforward is strictly functorial, $((j_n\circ i_{n-1})_*\mathcal H)(V)=\mathcal H(i_{n-1}^{-1}j_n^{-1}V)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], so $j_{n,*}i_{n-1,*}=j_{n-1,*}$ on $\mathcal O_{X_{n-1}}$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem) (the diagram of the X_n and the maps i_n)

proof.text: (2), the functor on objects. Let $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ be an object of $\mathrm{Sys}$ and $\mathcal G_n=j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ ($n\ge1$). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1) (for the closed immersion $j_{n-1}$ of locally Noetherian schemes, ideal sheaf $\mathcal I^n$, step 2) $\mathcal G_n$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_n=0$. Let $\eta$ be the unit of $i_{n-1}^*\dashv i_{n-1,*}$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; the map adjoint to $\varphi_{n-1}$ is $\tau_n=i_{n-1,*}(\varphi_{n-1})\circ\eta_{\mathcal F_n}:\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] (closed immersion $i_{n-1}$ with ideal $\mathcal I_n^n$, step 3) $\eta_{\mathcal F_n}$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n$, and $\varphi_{n-1}$ is an isomorphism, so $\tau_n$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n$ and induces an isomorphism $\bar\tau_n:\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$. The transition map is $t_n=j_{n,*}\tau_n:\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-ideal-powers] (3) (closed immersion $j_n$, ideal $\mathcal I$ of $X$, $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_n}=\mathcal I_n$ by step 3; $\mathcal F_n$ is quasi-coherent by step 2), $j_{n,*}$ of the quotient map $q:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n$ induces an isomorphism $\rho:\mathcal G_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to j_{n,*}(\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n)$. Since $t_n=j_{n,*}(\bar\tau_n)\circ j_{n,*}(q)$, the map $\mathcal G_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ induced by $t_n$ is $j_{n,*}(\bar\tau_n)\circ\rho$, an isomorphism. So $(\mathcal G_n,t_n)_{n\ge1}$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1).

(2), the functor on morphisms; full faithfulness. A morphism $(u_n):(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)\to(\mathcal F'_n,\varphi'_n)$ of $\mathrm{Sys}$ is sent to $(j_{n-1,*}u_{n-1})_{n\ge1}$. For any family of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-linear $u_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F'_n$, naturality of the unit and of the adjunction bijection $\psi\mapsto i_{n-1,*}\psi\circ\eta$ [def-pc-module-pullback] give $\tau'_n\circ u_n=i_{n-1,*}(\varphi'_{n-1}\circ i_{n-1}^*u_n)\circ\eta_{\mathcal F_n}$ and $i_{n-1,*}(u_{n-1})\circ\tau_n=i_{n-1,*}(u_{n-1}\circ\varphi_{n-1})\circ\eta_{\mathcal F_n}$; as the adjunction map is bijective, $\tau'_nu_n=i_{n-1,*}(u_{n-1})\tau_n$ holds if and only if $u_{n-1}\varphi_{n-1}=\varphi'_{n-1}\,i_{n-1}^*u_n$. Since $j_{n,*}$ is faithful [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful], the former holds if and only if $t'_n\circ j_{n,*}u_n=j_{n-1,*}u_{n-1}\circ t_n$. Hence $(u_n)\mapsto(j_{n-1,*}u_{n-1})$ is well defined (a functor $\Phi:\mathrm{Sys}\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$) and injective on morphisms; and for a morphism $(\alpha_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1) between the images there are unique $u_{n-1}$ with $j_{n-1,*}u_{n-1}=\alpha_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful], which by the equivalence just shown form a morphism of $\mathrm{Sys}$. So $\Phi$ is fully faithful.

(2), essential surjectivity. Let $(\mathcal G_n,t_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. For $n\ge0$, $\mathcal G_{n+1}$ is coherent with $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal G_{n+1}=0$, i.e. killed by the ideal sheaf of $j_n$ (step 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1) there are a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module $\mathcal F_n$ and an isomorphism $\beta_{n+1}:j_{n,*}\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $\beta_n^{-1}t_n\beta_{n+1}:j_{n,*}\mathcal F_n\to j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}=j_{n,*}i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ (step 3) is $j_{n,*}\tau_n$ for a unique $\tau_n:\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful]; let $\varphi_{n-1}:i_{n-1}^*\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_{n-1}$ be its adjoint, $\tau_n=i_{n-1,*}(\varphi_{n-1})\circ\eta_{\mathcal F_n}$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] $\eta_{\mathcal F_n}$ induces an isomorphism $\bar\eta:\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I_n^n\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}i_{n-1}^*\mathcal F_n$, so $\tau_n=\bar\tau_n\circ q$ with $\bar\tau_n=i_{n-1,*}(\varphi_{n-1})\circ\bar\eta$. As in step 4, with $\rho$ from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-ideal-powers] (3), the map $\mathcal G_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}\to\mathcal G_n$ induced by $t_n$ (an isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1)) equals $\beta_n\circ j_{n,*}(\bar\tau_n)\circ\rho\circ\bar\beta_{n+1}^{-1}$, $\bar\beta_{n+1}$ the isomorphism induced by $\beta_{n+1}$ on the quotients by $\mathcal I^n$ (an $\mathcal O_X$-linear isomorphism maps $\mathcal I^n j_{n,*}\mathcal F_n$ onto $\mathcal I^n\mathcal G_{n+1}$). Hence $j_{n,*}(\bar\tau_n)$ is an isomorphism; a fully faithful functor reflects isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful], so $\bar\tau_n$, then $i_{n-1,*}(\varphi_{n-1})=\bar\tau_n\bar\eta^{-1}$, then $\varphi_{n-1}$ are isomorphisms. Thus $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ is an object of $\mathrm{Sys}$, and $(\beta_n)_{n\ge1}:\Phi(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ ($t_n\beta_{n+1}=\beta_nj_{n,*}\tau_n$ by construction). A fully faithful essentially surjective functor is an equivalence; this proves (2).

(3), the system of restrictions. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, hence quasi-coherent of finite type (step 2). Then $j_n^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3), hence coherent on the Noetherian $X_n$ [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The isomorphisms $c_n:i_n^*j_{n+1}^*\mathcal F\cong j_n^*\mathcal F$ are the canonical isomorphisms $(j_{n+1}i_n)^*\cong i_n^*j_{n+1}^*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback], natural in $\mathcal F$; so $(\mathcal F|_{X_n},c_n)$ is an object of $\mathrm{Sys}$ and, for $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, $(u|_{X_n})_n=(j_n^*u)_n$ is a morphism of $\mathrm{Sys}$.

(3), the isomorphism with $\mathcal F^\wedge$. For $m\ge0$ let $\eta^{(m)}_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to j_{m,*}j_m^*\mathcal F$ be the unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] (ideal sheaf of $j_m$ is $\mathcal I^{m+1}$, step 2) it is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I^{m+1}\mathcal F$, so it induces an isomorphism $\rho_m:\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{m+1}\mathcal F\to j_{m,*}j_m^*\mathcal F$, natural in $\mathcal F$ (naturality of the unit). The transition map of $\Phi(\mathcal F|_{X_\bullet},c)$ is $t_n=j_{n,*}(i_{n-1,*}(c_{n-1})\circ\eta^{i_{n-1}}_{j_n^*\mathcal F})$ (step 4). The canonical isomorphism $c_{n-1}$ is, by definition, the isomorphism of left adjoints of $j_{n,*}i_{n-1,*}=j_{n-1,*}$ [def-pc-module-pullback], i.e. the one for which the unit of the composite adjunction, $j_{n,*}(\eta^{i_{n-1}}_{j_n^*\mathcal F})\circ\eta^{(n)}_{\mathcal F}$ followed by $j_{n-1,*}(c_{n-1})$, is $\eta^{(n-1)}_{\mathcal F}$; so $t_n\circ\eta^{(n)}_{\mathcal F}=\eta^{(n-1)}_{\mathcal F}$. Composing with the quotient maps, $t_n\circ\rho_n\circ\pi_{n+1}=\rho_{n-1}\circ\pi_n=\rho_{n-1}\circ s_n\circ\pi_{n+1}$, with $\pi_k:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^k\mathcal F$ and $s_n$ the canonical surjection $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$; as $\pi_{n+1}$ is an epimorphism, $t_n\rho_n=\rho_{n-1}s_n$. Hence $(\rho_{n-1})_{n\ge1}:\mathcal F^\wedge\to\Phi(\mathcal F|_{X_\bullet},c)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2), natural in $\mathcal F$; these are the isomorphisms $j_{n,*}j_n^*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F$ of the statement.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); the completion functor, equation 0880 (equation-completion-functor)

proof.text: (3), consequences. Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent. The families $(u_n:\mathcal G|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n})$ with $u_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$ are exactly the morphisms $(\mathcal G|_{X_\bullet},c)\to(\mathcal F|_{X_\bullet},c)$ of $\mathrm{Sys}$; by the full faithfulness of $\Phi$ (step 5) and the isomorphisms $\rho$ of step 8, $(u_n)\mapsto\rho^{\mathcal F}{}^{-1}\circ\Phi(u_n)\circ\rho^{\mathcal G}$ is a bijection onto $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)}(\mathcal G^\wedge,\mathcal F^\wedge)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1). For $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$, naturality of $\rho$ gives $\Phi(u|_{X_\bullet})\circ\rho^{\mathcal G}=\rho^{\mathcal F}\circ u^\wedge$, so $(u|_{X_n})_n$ corresponds to $u^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2). Similarly, for an object $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ of $\mathrm{Sys}$, isomorphisms $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong\Phi(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ correspond (composing with $\rho^{\mathcal F}$, and $\Phi$ fully faithful, so it reflects isomorphisms) to isomorphisms $(\psi_n):(\mathcal F|_{X_\bullet},c)\to(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ of $\mathrm{Sys}$, i.e. isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\psi_n\circ c_n=\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}$ (a morphism of $\mathrm{Sys}$ all of whose components are isomorphisms is an isomorphism of $\mathrm{Sys}$: the inverses satisfy the compatibility). This proves (3).

(4), supports. Let $\mathcal F_0$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module; it is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $Z=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2) is closed in $X_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (1) (closed immersion $j_0$ of locally Noetherian schemes), $\operatorname{Supp}(j_{0,*}\mathcal F_0)=j_0(Z)$, a closed subset of $X$ since $j_0$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $j_0(X_0)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The structure morphism $X_0\to S_0$ is the base change of $X\to S$, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], so 'proper over $S_0$' is defined for closed subsets of $X_0$.

(4), properness over $S_0$ versus over $S$. Choose a closed immersion $w:W\to X_0$ with $w(W)=Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]; $j_0\circ w$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] with image $j_0(Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] (1) ('for some closed subscheme structure'), applied to $X_0\to S_0$ and to $X\to S$: $Z$ is proper over $S_0$ iff $p:W\to X_0\to S_0$ is proper, and $j_0(Z)$ is proper over $S$ iff $W\to X\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]; the latter composite is $k\circ p$, where $k:S_0\to S$ (as $X_0\to X\to S$ equals $X_0\to S_0\to S$, the fibre product square). The morphism $k$ is a closed immersion ([lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1) for $\operatorname{id}_S$ and $K=I$: $S\times_SS_0\to S$ is $k$), hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c) and separated [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (a). If $p$ is proper, so is $k\circ p$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a). If $k\circ p$ is proper, then $p$ is proper because $k$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated]. So $Z$ is proper over $S_0$ iff $j_0(Z)$ is proper over $S$.

proof.text: (4), conclusion. By [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (4), an object $(\mathcal G_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ lies in $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ iff $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G_1)$ is proper over $S$. For $\Phi(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ we have $\mathcal G_1=j_{0,*}\mathcal F_0$, so by steps 10 and 11 it lies in that subcategory iff $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$. Isomorphic objects of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ have isomorphic first terms, hence the same support (isomorphic stalks [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2)), so the subcategory is closed under isomorphism and the equivalence $\Phi$ of (2) restricts to an equivalence from the full subcategory of the systems with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ proper over $S_0$ onto $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$. This proves (4).
